hints: Focus on counting two separate totals for each dot-and-cross structure, electrons shared in bonds versus electrons kept as lone pairs.
Remember each single bond contributes 2 bonding electrons and each double bond contributes 4, while each lone pair dot pair is 2 lone-pair electrons.
Draw $CO_2$ as $O=C=O$ and add up the electrons on the two oxygens, then compare that lone-pair total to the bonding total.
walkthrough:
**Recall what to count**

Bonding electrons are the shared electrons in covalent bonds. Lone-pair electrons are the non-bonding electrons left on each atom.

Rule to use:
$$\text{bonding electrons} = 2 \times \text{number of single bonds} + 4 \times \text{number of double bonds}$$

**Check CO2 structure**

Carbon dioxide is linear $O=C=O$ with two double bonds and no lone pair on carbon.

Calculation:
$$\text{bonding} = 2 \times 4 = 8 \text{ electrons}$$

**Count lone pairs in CO2**

Each oxygen in $O=C=O$ has an octet with 2 bonding pairs and 2 lone pairs. Carbon has no lone pair.

Calculation:
$$\text{lone-pair} = 2 \text{ O atoms} \times 2 \text{ pairs} \times 2 = 8 \text{ electrons}$$

**Conclude the match**

For $CO_2$, bonding electrons (8) equals lone-pair electrons (8). The other molecules give very different totals, so this is the one you want.

options.A: Incorrect. $BH_3$ has 3 single $B-H$ bonds, so 6 bonding electrons, but boron has an incomplete octet with no lone pair and hydrogen has no lone pair, so 0 lone-pair electrons.
options.B: Correct. $CO_2$ ($O=C=O$) has 2 double bonds giving 8 bonding electrons. Each O holds 2 lone pairs (4 electrons), giving 8 lone-pair electrons in total. The two totals are equal.
options.C: Incorrect. $F_2O$ ($F-O-F$) has 2 single bonds giving only 4 bonding electrons, but oxygen has 2 lone pairs and each fluorine has 3 lone pairs, giving 16 lone-pair electrons in total.
options.D: Incorrect. $SO_2$ is bent with a lone pair on sulfur. It has 8 bonding electrons if drawn with two $S=O$ double bonds, but 8 lone-pair electrons on the oxygens plus 2 on sulfur (10 total), so lone-pair electrons exceed bonding electrons.
